title: Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
web_title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix
book_title: Prologue: The Business, The Price & Our Independent Verdict
question: What does PROV do, what do we conclude, what would make us wrong, and what should you do with new money?

epigraph.quote: “Price is what you pay; value is what you get.”
epigraph.author: Benjamin Graham, as quoted by Warren Buffett in the 2008 Berkshire Hathaway shareholder letter

book_paragraphs: Let me give you the answer first, the way I would across a desk. Proventus Agrocom buys almonds, cashews and other dry fruits, packs them in Navi Mumbai and Surat, and sells them mostly under its ProV brand. About 72% of sales now carry that label. The rest is the older bulk and white-label trade that the founders started with. For new money, my verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. You do not own the stock, so there is nothing to hold or sell.

The shares closed at ₹2,125.70 on Friday 13 November 2026, a new 52-week high, after ₹2,061.00 on the 12th. I would not buy at either price. I would start buying in a zone of ₹1,850 to ₹1,875, and above the 50-day average at ₹1,900.75 I would do nothing. A weekly close below ₹1,692.11 would end the idea. My twelve-month base value is ₹2,216, so from today’s price there is barely 4% on offer against a stop that is 20% away.

I must be plain about dates, because they matter here. The half-year results for the period to 30 September were filed at about six in the evening on the 13th. The market had closed at half past three. So neither closing price has seen them, and the first day that can react is Monday 16 November. My numbers already include the results. What I cannot know is how the crowd will take them. The ledger I use for your portfolio and market regime is from the 12th, and the price snapshot is from the 13th. I name both so that you can see which is which.

Here is the bull case in a few sentences. Revenue grew 62.5% in the half. Brand sales rose 61% on 55% more volume, Surat Phase 1 is running, and the chart has held above its long average for 32 weeks. If the profit margin merely creeps from 1.6% to 2.2% while sales rise by half again, earnings per share reach about ₹103, and at 38 times that is ₹3,902. Management has beaten its own revenue promises. That is a fair reason to follow the stock.

Here is the bear case. The same half-year shows operating cash flow of minus ₹57.6 crore, receivables that doubled and net debt of about ₹51 crore where there was net cash last March. The CEO says growth needs “the ability to convert earnings into healthy cash flows over time.” I agree, and it has been shown for one cycle. Trading is thin, at a median of 320 shares a day. At 38 times earnings, the stock already pays for a lot of good news. In my bear case the price falls to ₹952.

I weigh those paths at 30% bear, 50% base and 20% bull. The weighted price is ₹2,174, only 2.3% above the close. That is why the plan is to wait. From ₹1,900 the reward-to-risk is 1.52 to one, and the expected gain is only 14.4%, so I rejected it as an entry. From ₹1,875 it is 1.86 to one, and from ₹1,850 it is 2.32 to one. Our gate is 1.5.

One more question deserves an answer: did I price the cost of funding the growth? I did. My base margins sit below the last half-year’s, which leaves room for about ₹34 crore of extra average debt. A share sale of about ₹50 crore would break the gate, and my base case includes none. That is what I would check first in the March balance sheet.

Judge the three horizons separately. For a short-term trader, wait: the momentum gauges are above 70, the results are unpriced and the tape cannot take size. For a medium-term investor, it is conditional on cash collection in the festive half and on Surat Phases 2 and 3 arriving by June 2027. For a long-term owner, it is potential but not proven, because the moat is narrow and the business funds only about 14% growth from its own cash.

Where does the spare money go? I looked at cash above your 10% ceiling, which is about ₹1,45,415. I would put roughly a quarter into the shortlist name AJMERA and keep three-quarters in cash. I would put nothing into an outside company, because I did not research one this time. If the price drops to the zone and the cash flow keeps improving, we revisit.

So here is your homework. Watch Monday’s reaction, but do not trade it. Set alerts at ₹1,875 and ₹1,850. Set a weekly alert at ₹1,692.11. Read the next result for receivables, borrowings and operating cash flow before anything else. Good businesses and good purchases are different things, and the second depends on the price you pay.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: You and I can like the company and still say no to the quote. The work is to write down the price, the stop and the evidence before the market tempts us. If the stock runs without us, we have lost a trade that never met our test and kept our capital.

web_blocks.html: Proventus Agrocom imports, packs and sells dry fruits and snacks, mostly under its ProV brand, which was about 72% of H1 FY27 revenue [2]. Revenue for the half was ₹633.3 crore at a PAT margin near 1.9% [1]. Our verdict for new capital is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT: no purchase at the ₹2,125.70 close, with an entry zone of ₹1,850 to ₹1,875. You hold no shares, so the holding action is NOT_HELD.

The levels are exact. The entry zone is ₹1,850 to ₹1,875, below the 50-day average of ₹1,900.75 and around the ₹1,864 pivot [71]. Above ₹1,900.75 we do nothing. The stop is a weekly close below ₹1,692.11. Our 12-month scenarios are ₹952 (bear, 30%), ₹2,216 (base, 50%) and ₹3,902 (bull, 20%), a weighted ₹2,174 or 2.3% above the close. Reward-to-risk is 0.21:1 at ₹2,125.70, 1.52:1 at ₹1,900, 1.86:1 at ₹1,875 and 2.32:1 at ₹1,850. The 1.5:1 gate passes by only 0.02 at ₹1,900, and the weighted return there is 14.4%, so we reject ₹1,900 as an entry. The tier is TIER_3 with a 2.0% to 3.5% weight band and a 50 bps risk budget.

Dating matters. The H1 FY27 results were filed at about 17:57 IST on 13 November, after the 15:30 close, so neither close reflects them [1][2]. The first session that can react is Monday 16 November. The ledger session is 12 November (close ₹2,061.00; regime uptrend with narrow breadth). The TradingView snapshot is the 13 November session (close ₹2,125.70, a new 52-week high of ₹2,150 on 2.77 times average volume) [71][73]. We use ₹2,125.70 as the CMP. Our valuation already includes the new half-year, so trailing EPS is ₹55.71 and the P/E is 38.2x, not the 52.0x shown before the results.

web_blocks.takeaway: The business verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL with KPI health PASS_WITH_WATCH; options are NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID.

web_blocks.html: The matrix shows one pattern. Every horizon is conditional, and each trigger is a price or a reported number, not a mood. The price triggers act on a thin tape, where the median volume is 320 shares a day, so a stop is an alert and not a guaranteed exit [73].

Financing is the check that could flip the verdict. Base margins sit below the H1 FY27 actual, which leaves a cushion that absorbs about ₹34 crore of extra average debt, so the base case holds to roughly ₹75 crore of average borrowings. It includes no equity raise. An equity raise near ₹50 crore, which dilutes holders by 6.8% and cuts the base price to ₹2,075, would fail the gate from ₹1,850, as would a base price of ₹2,087 or lower. Chapter 9 sets out the working. If borrowings exceed ₹75 crore at 31 March 2027, or equity is raised, we re-run the gate [1][3].

The bull case: revenue rose 62.5% in the half, brand sales rose 61% on 55% more volume, and Surat Phase 1 is operational [2][3]. If PAT margin creeps from 1.6% to 2.2% while sales rise about 45% to 50%, trailing EPS reaches ₹102.7, and at 38 times that is ₹3,902. The stock has also stayed above a rising 30-week average for 32 weeks.

The bear case: operating cash flow was minus ₹57.64 crore in H1 FY27, receivables doubled to ₹78.56 crore, and net cash of about ₹19.6 crore became net debt near ₹51 crore [1][3]. Own cash funds only about 14% growth a year, against a brand guide near 29%. At 38.2 times trailing earnings, PROV trades above LT Foods at 22.5 times with less than a quarter of its operating margin [72]. In our bear case the price falls to ₹952 and a stop may not fill on this tape.

Redeployment follows the next marginal cash unit. Of the ₹1,45,415 above the 10% cash ceiling, 25% goes to the shortlist name AJMERA, conditional on it still sitting near its support zone when the money moves, 0% to any outside candidate and 75% stays in cash, because PROV fails the gate at today’s price and AJMERA is the only shortlist name whose own dossier calls for an immediate buy at the live price. Its ledger Stage is 3 while its snapshot and dossier say Stage 2, so the slice is conditional on re-confirming that Stage. MANORAMA sits 1.9% above its entry zone, and ZYDUSLIFE is inside its zone but its own verdict is still WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT at a thin 1.56:1. Alerts to set: ₹1,875 and ₹1,850 for the entry zone, a weekly close at ₹1,692.11 for invalidation, and ₹2,216 as the base target. A spike above ₹2,150 on Monday is not a buy signal.
